newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T dips after latest U.S. court ruling.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T dips after latest U.S. court ruling.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc were down 3-1/2p to 513 by 0730 GMT following news late Wednesday that a U.S. judge had reinstated a class-action shareholder suit against Philip Morris Cos Inc.

U.S. District Judge Michael Mukasey said he had restored the suit, orginally dismissed in 1995, because of the recent emergence of documents that present new evidence of alleged misrepresentations and omissions by the tobacco company.
"Litigation is a cost of doing business in the U.S. But when you start having investors taking you to court, that can't be good news," the head of trading of a major investment bank said.
"But the market is getting used to these sorts of shocks coming out of the U.S. Once thing quieten down a bit, people will probably start buying tobaccos on the dips."
Dealers do not expect the news to have a major impact on B.A.T's share price today noting that tobacco stocks suffered only modest losses in New York overnight.
Philip Morris shares lost just $3/4 to $113-5/8, while RJR Nabisco Holdings Inc eased $1/4 to $30-3/8, in-line with a weaker Wall Street where the Dow ended 45 points lower on Wednesday.

In the lawsuit, which names Philip Morris and four company executives as defendants, the plaintiffs said the company artificially inflated the stock price by maintaining the public stance "that nicotine is not addictive (and) that smoking is entirely a matter of 'choice.'"

In his latest opinion, the judge cited newly discovered evidence that specifically identified Philip Morris and tobacco industry documents discussing studies concerning whether cigarettes and nicotine are addictive.

"This new documentary evidence is of enough potential importance and volume that I probably would not have granted defendants' motion to dismiss had it been described in the initial complaint," Mukasey said, adding, "Most of this evidence is admissible."
B.A.T Industries, along with other major tobacco companies, is currently involved in a plethora of lawsuits in the U.S. but is not a defendant in this particular class action lawsuit.
